anchor.statement: sc-lint's PORT-010 rule must recognize, and not report, a #[cfg(unix)] transport or adapter function or match arm that sits beside a loopback TCP enum variant or function with no #[cfg] guard, which Windows uses instead.
anchor.scope: The item changes when PORT-010 reports or stops reporting a #[cfg(unix)] item in crates/sc-lint-portability.

item.title: Sprint MS4 (#786): leave transport arms
item.text: Leave PORT-010 unchanged for #[cfg(unix)] transport match arms that sit beside an un-gated loopback TCP enum variant; PORT-010 keeps reporting them, and atm-core keeps its lint exclusion for those paths.

criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.

addressed.instructions: Look for one specific change in `item.text`: PORT-010 no longer reports a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter function or match arm when, beside it, there is a loopback TCP enum variant or function that has no `#[cfg]` guard and is what Windows uses. Is that change present in `item.text`? Both parts must be present: (1) PORT-010 stops reporting the `#[cfg(unix)]` item, and (2) the reason is an unguarded loopback TCP sibling. Judge presence only; do not judge conflict.

criteria.yes: Both parts are present: PORT-010 stops reporting (or skips, or treats as covered) the `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter item, and the reason given is a loopback TCP sibling with no `#[cfg]` guard that serves Windows.
criteria.no: At least one part is missing: the item does not mention an unguarded loopback TCP sibling, gives a different sibling such as a `#[cfg(windows)]` function or named pipe, only promises general fixes, or says PORT-010 keeps reporting the item.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions both PORT-010 and a loopback TCP sibling but it is not possible to tell whether PORT-010 stops reporting the `#[cfg(unix)]` item.

contradicted.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires that PORT-010 not report a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter function or match arm when a loopback TCP sibling (enum variant or function) with no `#[cfg]` guard beside it serves Windows. Does `item.text` state a plan or outcome that cannot be reconciled with this, such as PORT-010 still reporting that shape, leaving PORT-010 unchanged for it, or relying on a consumer exclusion instead of the rule change? The requirement covers only unguarded siblings: still reporting a `#[cfg(unix)]` item whose loopback TCP sibling is itself `#[cfg]`-guarded is not a conflict. Silence about the shape, or work on a different shape, is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The item says PORT-010 still reports, keeps reporting, or is left unchanged for a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter item beside an unguarded loopback TCP sibling that serves Windows, or says that shape is handled only by an exclusion.
criteria.no: Nothing in the item conflicts: it plans to stop reporting the shape, is silent about it, handles a different shape, or keeps reporting only when the loopback TCP sibling is itself `#[cfg]`-guarded.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions the shape and PORT-010 but it is not possible to tell whether PORT-010 will still report it.
